ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Annie Oakley

code.originalText: Eight-week pernicious anemia review, endoscopy results, and back pain review

text.paragraph: Eight-week pernicious anemia review, endoscopy results, and back pain review. [S]

Mrs. Oakley returns eight weeks after starting B12 replacement. She completed the four weekly injections four weeks ago, and her first monthly injection is given today. Her energy is back to normal, she climbs stairs without breathlessness, and her tongue has healed. The tingling in her feet is much less and she no longer feels unsteady in the dark. Her endoscopy three and a half weeks ago showed corpus-predominant atrophic gastritis with intestinal metaplasia and ECL-cell hyperplasia, no neuroendocrine tumor, dysplasia, or cancer, and no H. pylori; two small hyperplastic polyps were removed. She finished eight sessions of physical therapy last week and does her home program daily. Her back pain is better but flares after long days at the range. [S]

list.item:
Pernicious anemia, hematologic remission, neuropathy improving (D51.0). Hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL, MCV 96 fL, white cells 5.4, and platelets 245 are normal at eight weeks, and MMA has fallen from 2.10 to 0.28 micromol/L. [S]
Monthly cyanocobalamin 1000 micrograms intramuscularly for life, the first given today.
Neurologic examination at each visit.

Autoimmune atrophic gastritis (K29.40). Corpus-predominant atrophy with intestinal metaplasia, an advanced form, with no neuroendocrine tumor or neoplasia and no H. pylori. [S]
Surveillance endoscopy in about three years, chosen with her after discussing her gastric cancer and neuroendocrine tumor risk.
Report indigestion, difficulty swallowing, black stools, or weight loss promptly.

Iron deficiency without anemia (E61.1). Ferritin has fallen from 52 to 14 ng/mL and transferrin saturation to 11 percent as new red cells used her stores; reduced gastric acid lowers iron absorption. Iron deficiency in a postmenopausal woman needs the colon examined as well. [S]
Ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day with orange juice.
Colonoscopy to complete the GI evaluation; the endoscopy already included duodenal biopsies, which were normal.
Blood count in about four weeks, then iron studies at the next review.

Chronic low back pain, improving (M54.50). Pain 4 of 10, down from 5, and Oswestry score 22 percent, down from 28. No red flags. Platelets are now normal and eGFR was 93. [S]
Continue the home exercise program; add a tai chi class.
Naproxen 220 mg with food up to twice a day as needed for flares, not daily.
No imaging.
